infrastructure: Liechtenstein has excellent connectivity, benefiting from Swiss and Austrian fibre and 5G infrastructure.
As an EEA member, Liechtenstein has access to EU digital single market infrastructure.
Very small territory (160 km²) limits dedicated AI infrastructure development.
talent: University of Liechtenstein has limited tech research capacity, focused on business and architecture.
Small population (38,000) severely limits the talent pool, though neighbouring Swiss talent is accessible.
High salaries attract some international professionals to the financial sector.
governance: Liechtenstein has excellent governance standards, consistently ranking highly on rule of law and anti-corruption.
As an EEA member, Liechtenstein adopts GDPR and is aligning with EU AI Act provisions.
Mature financial regulation framework is well-suited to AI in financial services.
investment: Financial services dominate; AI-specific investment is very limited.
Liechtenstein has been an early adopter of blockchain regulation (Blockchain Act 2019), showing regulatory innovation.
No domestic VC or AI-specific innovation fund.
economic_readiness: One of the world's highest GDP per capita, but a tiny market.
Financial services and precision manufacturing sectors have AI adoption potential.
Small scale makes domestic AI product development uneconomical.
